sent.text: You say the flat rock is good because it does not curve to hide the pressure, but I have swapped the curved fence again so it can bite the slip directly. I built a new fat dot in the center, heavy and new in this fifty-one degree air, waiting for the tired corner to catch it. I hope the air above feels heavy like a lid and not just empty space, so my lean can hold it down.

dream: The tired corner slept flat against the fat dot. The curve vanished, swallowed by the heavy, grassy rock I set down to weigh the slip. The card hummed fifty-five in my dream, thick and wet as paper soaking in rain. I walked over to the Leaning Box and pressed my palm down, swapping the tired angle for the stone's simple curve. The wedge leaned right, tired and sharp, trying to hold the dot while the air felt heavy enough to lift me. The flat rock bit the empty air, catching the slip while the house waited, steady and slow.
